files.evidence: Read in full (607 lines). The pool is keyed only by agentId (562-605) despite the module describing agent/workspace state, while index.js calls get(agentId) and hydrates only once from the first workspace file (index.js:5629-5655). Thus mood can cross workspace boundaries. applyEmotionScore accepts any truthy nuance label into nuanceState (134-158), hydrateOnce restores arbitrary labels from JSON (422-445), and describe/format functions emit unknown labels without prompt escaping (310-359, 525-552). The packaged emotional-state injector then interpolates label/nuances directly into prompt instructions (.openclaw/extensions/emotional-state-injector/index.js:52-67). Validation must determine upstream label allowlisting and writer trust.

Read in full (475 lines). Conversation turns are embedded in an LLM prompt without an explicit untrusted-data instruction (246-278); parsed title/narrativeArc/turningPoint/summary are accepted without enum/length/type validation (280-299), stored in Neo and automatically written after agent_end (index.js:4710-4735). writeEpisodeToVault sanitizes the filename slug but writes generated values verbatim into YAML/Markdown (334-420), so newline-bearing fields can forge frontmatter or prompt-like note content. Obsidian scanning treats generic notes as review-only by default, reducing but not eliminating the persistent-content boundary. LLM/parse catches at 283-297 and recall catch at 464-468 are silent; episodic recall is also a placeholder-only feature.

Read in full (63 lines). It reads only local perf_hooks histogram metrics and exposes no untrusted input or privileged output. Multiple silent catches violate observability rules but only disable telemetry.

Read in full (126 lines). Pure arithmetic/rendering helpers; no file, query, process, network, authorization, or model-tool sink. Non-finite component values can produce misleading percentages, a correctness validation gap only.

Read in full (254 lines). Feedback enum is enforced (51-63), logs are capped at 5,000 and atomically rewritten (14-16, 39-49, 124-168), and runtime command use records feedback without enabling dynamics (index.js:4185). The optional dynamics path does not call safeUuid/safeAgentId itself (77-109), but its only production caller omits dbPool/agentId so it is dormant. Fixed .tmp filenames are race-prone and negative-query reports retain raw query text, both functional/privacy-hardening concerns.

rawCandidates.title: Emotional state is isolated by agent but not by workspace
rawCandidates.source: Conversation emotion from any workspace served by an agent updates emotionalPool.get(agentId).
rawCandidates.control: The pool key and hydrate-once guard omit workspace identity.
rawCandidates.sink: The shared state affects recall boosting, serialized mood files, and prompt/style injection in later turns for the same agent in another workspace.
rawCandidates.impact: A workspace can infer or inherit another workspace's emotional state and have its recall/response behavior influenced across the intended isolation boundary.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Pool-key omission is confirmed. Validate whether one long-lived plugin instance can handle the same agentId across distinct ctx.workspaceKey/workspaceDir values and whether recall uses this exact pool state.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires access to one of multiple workspaces sharing an agent process/ID; sending emotionally salient text changes state that the other workspace later consumes.

rawCandidates.title: Unvalidated mood labels and nuances are interpolated into prompt instructions
rawCandidates.source: Emotion-engine output or persisted .emotional-state.json supplies nuance labels/state.
rawCandidates.control: Intensities are clamped, but unknown labels are retained and no text/attribute sanitizer is applied before formatting.
rawCandidates.sink: The packaged emotional-state injector places label and nuances into a before_prompt_build instruction block, including an instruction to reproduce a generated display line.
rawCandidates.impact: If upstream classification or a writable workspace state file can introduce control text/newlines, persistent prompt instructions can be injected into later model turns.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Sink is confirmed. Validate emotion-score/engine label schemas, actual file-writer provenance, newline handling, extension activation, and whether OpenClaw treats the block as higher-trust context.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires either prompt influence over a configured emotion LLM that can emit an unallowlisted label or write access to the workspace mood state; ordinary known emotion labels are harmless.

rawCandidates.title: Episode LLM output is persisted as unsanitized Neo and YAML/Markdown metadata
rawCandidates.source: Untrusted conversation turns influence narrative LLM JSON fields.
rawCandidates.control: JSON parsing exists and filename characters are stripped, but field types, lengths, enum membership, newlines, and YAML quoting are not validated.
rawCandidates.sink: Generated episode metadata is appended to Neo storage and written verbatim into an automatically generated Markdown note/frontmatter.
rawCandidates.impact: A crafted conversation/model response can forge note metadata or plant prompt-like persistent content that enters later review, graph, or recall workflows.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: Source-to-persistence is complete. Validate downstream Neo episode consumers, Obsidian classification/approval requirements, Markdown/YAML parser behavior, and model prompt priority.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires at least five turns and configured LLM narrative enrichment; the attacker influences source text, while successful field injection depends on the LLM following embedded instructions or being compromised.

notes: Three candidates retained for later validation. No feature-disable remedy is needed: scope mood state by agent+workspace and schema/sanitize generated labels/episode metadata while keeping emotion and episode features active.
